owns: LeaveRequest model (id, employeeId, leaveType, startDate, endDate, days, reason, status, managerId, reviewedAt, reviewedBy, createdAt, updatedAt)

recommended_phases.title: Phase 1: Foundation — leave-type enum + audit-log module
recommended_phases.rationale: These two modules have zero internal dependencies. leave-type defines the shared LeaveType enum (annual, sick, emergency) used by every other module. audit-log provides the cross-cutting IAuditService interface and repository required by GP-002. Both must exist before any dependent module is built.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 2: Policy engine — leave-policy module
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends only on leave-type. Defines policy rules (max days, notice hours, approval requirements) that gate every leave application. The ILeavePolicyService.validateRequest method is the single entry point for policy enforcement. Must exist before leave-request can validate applications.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 3: Balance tracker — leave-balance module
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends on leave-type and audit-log. Manages the balance ledger: deduct on approval, restore on rejection/cancellation, accrue periodically. The ILeaveBalanceService is called by leave-request during the approval/rejection workflow. Building it before leave-request avoids forward references.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 4: Request workflow — leave-request module (service + repository)
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends on leave-type, leave-policy, leave-balance, and audit-log. This is the orchestrator: applyLeave validates against policy, checks balance, creates the request, and writes audit. approveLeave/rejectLeave delegate to balance and audit. This is the largest phase — keep it to the service interface, service implementation, and repository.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 5: API surface — controllers + routes for all modules
recommended_phases.rationale: With all services built, expose REST endpoints. Each module gets its own controller (input validation per GP-003) and route registration. RBAC enforcement (GP-005) is applied at the route level: employees can apply/cancel their own leave; managers can approve/reject for their team; HR admins can configure policies.

app_notes:
## Application Layer Design — Leave Management Module

### Layer boundaries

| Layer | Modules | Responsibility |
|-------|---------|----------------|
| **Domain** | `leave-type` | Shared enum — no logic, no deps |
| **Domain** | `leave-request` (model), `leave-balance` (model), `leave-policy` (model), `audit-log` (model) | Pure data shapes |
| **Application** | `ILeaveRequestService`, `ILeaveBalanceService`, `ILeavePolicyService`, `IAuditService` | Service interfaces — the contract layer |
| **Infrastructure** | `*.repository.ts` files inside each module | Data access (GP-001), PostgreSQL via the shared `pool` |
| **Presentation** | `*.controller.ts` + `*.routes.ts` (Phase 5) | Fastify route handlers with RBAC (GP-005) and input validation (GP-003) |

### Dependency direction (all inward)

```
leave-type ◄── leave-policy ◄── leave-request
     ▲                              ▲
     └──────── leave-balance ───────┘
                    ▲
               audit-log
```

- `leave-type` and `audit-log` are zero-dependency leaves
- `leave-policy` depends only on `leave-type`
- `leave-balance` depends on `leave-type` + `audit-log`
- `leave-request` is the orchestrator, depending on all four

### Golden Principles coverage

- **GP-001 (Repository pattern)**: Every module has its own repository; services call repositories, never the DB directly
- **GP-002 (Audit records)**: `IAuditService` is injected into `leave-request` and `leave-balance` services; every state change (apply, approve, reject, cancel, deduct, restore, accrue) writes an audit record
- **GP-003 (Input validation)**: Controllers (Phase 5) validate all inputs at the API boundary
- **GP-005 (RBAC enforcement)**: Route registration applies role checks — employee (own requests), manager (team approvals), HR admin (policy config)
- **GP-006 (Error handling)**: All async service methods use try/catch; Fastify error handler catches unhandled rejections

### Phase decomposition rationale

Phases are ordered by dependency so each phase can be built, tested, and merged independently. Each phase fits within Aider's effective context window (max 5 files per phase per `HARNESS.json` planner config).
